segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Thanks for turning up today, thanks for turning up toddy to this short talk I’m going to give on student banking.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Many of you are unfamiliar with the way banks work in this country and today’s talk should just give you a few starting points.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I will of course answer any questions at the end.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Right.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Well ,as you probably know, you’ll need to open a bank account while you’re here — it’s the safest place to keep your money and it’s best to open an account with one of the major banks.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You should each have a handout with the names and addresses … there’s Barclays in Realty Square, National Westminster in Preston Park, Lloyds in City Plaza and Midland in Hope Street.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: OK.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: All these banks offer special student accounts.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: However, it’s important to note that as an international student you’ll not necessarily be eligible for all the facilities offered to resident students.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Now, as an international student you will need to provide evidence that you can fund yourself for however long your course lasts.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Banks have different policies and the services that they’ll offer you will depend on your individual circumstances and on the discretion of the bank manager involved.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So it’s a matter of going there and finding out about your own particular situation.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Right, erm, when you do go to open a bank account, you should take some documentation with you.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I’ve already mentioned that you must be able to support yourself.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In addition to this most banks ask you to bring your passport and your letter or certificate of enrolment.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: OK?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Now, by far the most useful type of account to open is a current account.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: When you do this, you will actually get what is called a “student account” which is a current account with special concessions for students.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: When you open the account, the bank will give you a chequebook and you can use this to draw money out as you need it.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: If you need to write cheques in shops, you’ll also need a cheque card.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This is really an identity card which guarantees that correctly written cheques up to the value stated on the card will be honoured by the bank.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: OK?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Right, er, if you want to draw out cash for yourself you can make the cheque payable in your own name or “to cash”.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You can also withdraw cash from a cashpoint machine with a cashcard.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: These are extremely useful as they enable you to withdraw cash from your account during the day or at night.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There is also another card called Switch or Delta and you can use this to pay for things in shops.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It takes the money right out of your account, so you don’t need your chequebook.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Now — you may want to take more money out of the bank than you have in it.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This is called having an overdraft.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Be very careful with this you should not do this without permission from your bank.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Overdrafts usually incur charges though some banks offer interest-free overdrafts to some students.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But find out before you get one!

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Right?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Well, that just leaves opening times — when can you go?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Banks used to be open from 9.30 am until 3.30 pm from Monday to Friday but many main branches are now open until 4.30 or 5 pm on weekdays and some of the bigger branches in London and other major cities are now open for a limited time on Saturdays.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: OK — any questions?
